title: PyPIM: Integrating Digital Processing-in-Memory from Microarchitectural Design to Python Tensors
problem: There is a significant gap between high-level programming models and microarchitectural design for digital processing-in-memory architectures, particularly for handling partitions and operations across both directions of the memory array in memristive PIM.
motivation: Digital PIM mitigates the memory wall by enabling parallel bitwise operations directly within memory, but lacks accessible programming abstractions to bridge hardware capabilities with high-level application development.
method: PyPIM proposes an efficient microarchitecture and ISA that bridges control periphery and PIM parallelism abstraction, a Python library that converts tensor operations to ISA instructions, and a PIM driver translating ISA to micro-operations. Evaluation uses cycle-accurate simulation across diverse benchmarks to demonstrate performance versus theoretical bounds.
key_novelty: End-to-end integration from high-level Python tensor library to microarchitectural design with compiler toolchain, eliminating the abstraction gap for memristive PIM programming.
contributions: Microarchitecture and ISA design for digital memristive PIM with support for cross-direction array operations
PIM development library converting high-level Python tensor operations to ISA instructions
PIM driver translating ISA to micro-operations
Cycle-accurate simulator framework enabling transparent conversion of existing tensor programs to PIM
